data.value: Every Worker on this Cloudflare account shares it, it has to be unique across all of Cloudflare, and it can be changed later in the dashboard under Workers & Pages, Account details. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.

data.value: Set automatically: today when you mark an order completed or cancelled, or the date the linked contract was accepted. Override it here if the real date differs.

data.name: PriorityPutThisOrder
data.value: Priority — put this order and everything it needs at the top

data.name: TipOutranksEveryOtherOrder
data.value: Outranks every other order regardless of estimated date, along with the jobs, purchases and hauls that serve it.

data.name: NormallyFilledInAutomaticallyNote
data.value: Normally filled in automatically — every contract carrying this order, since an order can go out over several. Add an id here when a contract cannot be matched, usually because it was made out before the order was entered; separate several with commas. Removing an id lets that contract go.

data.name: FreeTagsForGroupingNote
data.value: Free tags for grouping orders — a corp programme, a customer, a shipment. Type anything; if it does not exist yet, pressing Enter creates it. The Order Tracker can filter on them.

data.value: Copy the raw formatted text (with markup) to the clipboard

data.name: TipIncludeSalesMarkedAs
data.value: Include sales marked as not for profit. They count everywhere on this screen when shown: the summaries, the charts and the grid all follow this box.

data.name: UsedForOrderStatusNote
data.value: Used for order status notifications, and for store requests when the EVE mail store is open.

data.name: GiveInStockOrders
data.value: Give in-stock orders an expected date

data.name: OrderLabelsOnEveryNote
data.value: ORDER LABELS (on every order this store takes)

data.name: LabelsAppearOnTheNote
data.value: Labels appear on the Order Tracker and can be filtered there. Anything typed here is offered in its label pickers, so a programme can be set up before its first order arrives.

data.name: UsedWhenServeIsNote
data.value: Used when Serve is set to List. A sender matches by their own name, their corporation, or their alliance. Names are resolved against ids the app has already seen.

data.name: AnyoneOrOnlyTheNote
data.value: Anyone, or only the list below. The same for EVE mail and the web site.

data.name: HintTypeTwoLettersOfThe
data.value: Type two letters of the name…
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in StoresView.

data.name: HowMuchOneBuyerNote
data.value: How much one buyer may take, counted over their orders in this store that were not cancelled, whichever doorway placed them. For a programme that hands out the first hull of each kind: one unit of each item type, all time. On the site an item a buyer may no longer order is greyed out and the units box holds what remains; an order over the limit that reaches the app anyway is held for you to look at, never booked on its own.

data.name: AShopFrontInNote
data.value: A shop front in the mailbox: buyers write to the character above and the app answers, books orders and keeps them posted. Who may buy is set on the Restrictions tab, the same for mail and the web.

data.name: OpenByEveMail
data.value: Open by EVE mail — read and answer mail sent to the mailbox

data.name: BuyersPutTheCommandNote
data.value: Buyers put the command in the mail SUBJECT: PRICES, ORDER, STATUS, CANCEL or HELP. An ORDER body is one item per line — dragging the item in is easiest. STATUS on its own lists every open order; CANCEL needs the reference from the confirmation mail.

data.name: MessageHeaderOnEveryNote
data.value: MESSAGE HEADER (on every mail this store sends)

data.name: HintEGThanksFor
data.value: e.g. Thanks for shopping with us.
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in StoresView.

data.name: TipEveMarkupWorksHere
data.value: EVE markup works here: <b>, <i>, <u>, dragged links, and [color=#rrggbb]text[/color]. The colour beside this box tints the whole block; the tag colours part of it.

data.name: BothAcceptEveMarkupNote
data.value: Both accept EVE markup — bold, italic, underline, dragged links — and [color=#rrggbb]text[/color] for part of a line. The picker beside each box tints the whole block.

data.name: HintEGContractsAre
data.value: e.g. Contracts are issued from Jita 4-4.
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in StoresView.

data.name: AShopFrontOnNote
data.value: A shop front on the web, on a site you host. Buyers sign in with EVE SSO, see this price list with what is in stock, in build and reserved, place orders and follow them. The app sends the site what it may show and collects what buyers did every few minutes; nothing on the site reaches the database. Who may buy is set on the Restrictions tab, the same for mail and the web.

data.name: OpenOnTheWeb
data.value: Open on the web — publish to the site and take its orders

data.name: MinutesABuyerWaitsNote
data.value: minutes. A buyer waits up to this long for a confirmation; every call is one of the site's free daily requests.

data.name: AlsoMailWebBuyers
data.value: Also mail web buyers as their orders move (needs the character above)

data.name: TheThemeIsTheNote
data.value: The theme is the store's own and has nothing to do with the theme this desktop is showing. The secret is what the app signs each call with; set the same value as the site's STORE_SYNC_SECRET when you set the site up by hand.

data.name: AboutThisStoreOnTheLabel
data.value: ABOUT THIS STORE, ON THE SITE

data.name: HintContractTermsPickupWhatever
data.value: Contract terms, pickup, whatever a buyer should read before ordering. Plain text or HTML.
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in StoresView.

data.name: HtmlIsWelcomeBNote
data.value:
HTML is welcome:

    1. and the mail markup's . Line breaks and blank lines are kept as written until you lay it out with paragraph or list tags, after which the tags decide. The site drops scripts, handlers and tags it does not know, and closes any tag left open.

data.name: OptionalShownAcrossTheNote
data.value: Optional. Shown across the top of the price list, the width of the page and up to 300 pixels tall; a wide picture, about 1100 by 250, fits best, and a taller one shows its middle. A big file is scaled down and sent as WebP.

data.name: EveApplicationNeededBeforeNote
data.value: EVE APPLICATION (needed before buyers can sign in)

data.name: DeployFirstSoTheNote
data.value: Deploy first, so the site has an address. Then register an application on the EVE developer site: any name and description, Authentication only (no scopes), and the callback address shown below. Copy its Client ID and Secret Key into the two boxes: a site deployed from here receives them the moment they are saved, and the line under the boxes says whether the site holds these keys. A site set up by hand needs the same values as its EVE_CLIENT_ID and EVE_CLIENT_SECRET secrets.

data.name: OpenDevelopersEveonlineCom
data.value: Open developers.eveonline.com to create the application

data.name: HintKnownOnceTheSite
data.value: Known once the site has an address, or an account and worker name below
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in StoresView.

data.name: HintFromTheApplicationsPage
data.value: From the application's page on the developer site
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in StoresView.

data.name: HintShownOnceWhenThe
data.value: Shown once, when the application is created
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in StoresView.

data.name: AutomaticDeploymentAndUpdatesNote
data.value: AUTOMATIC DEPLOYMENT AND UPDATES ON CLOUDFLARE (only for the Deploy button)

data.name: FillTheseInOnlyNote
data.value: Fill these in only to have the app put the site on your own Cloudflare account and keep it current with the Deploy or update site button: it creates the database, uploads the newest release of the site, sets the secrets above and puts it on the free workers.dev address or a domain of your own on that account. Deploying again updates the site without touching its orders. To set the site up by hand instead, follow the documentation, then enter the site address and secret above; none of these fields is needed for that.

data.name: OnTheCloudflareTokenNote
data.value: On the Cloudflare token page: Create Token, the “Edit Cloudflare Workers” template, add the permission D1 Edit, then Continue and Create. Paste it below and press Save token; it is checked, then kept on this machine only, encrypted for your account.

data.name: HintPasteATokenTo
data.value: Paste a token to save it on this machine
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in StoresView.

data.name: HintSaveATokenToList
data.value: Save a token to list accounts
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in StoresView.

data.name: AlsoTheDatabasesNameNote
data.value: Also the database's name. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens; the site's address is this name on the account's workers.dev unless a domain of your own is chosen below.

data.name: TheFreeWorkersDev
data.value: The free workers.dev address: the worker name on the account's workers.dev

data.name: ADomainOfMy2
data.value: A domain of my own on Cloudflare:

data.name: ADomainMustAlreadyNote
data.value: A domain must already be on this Cloudflare account with its DNS there. The next Deploy attaches the site to it, Cloudflare makes the record and the certificate, and the workers.dev address is switched off so buyers and the EVE application's callback see one name; switching back lets the domain go. Either way the callback URL above changes, so update the EVE application to match.

data.name: WhatInfoSendsBackNote
data.value: What INFO sends back: who runs the store, what it stocks, delivery terms, whatever a buyer should know before ordering. Leave it empty and the command is not offered — the usage message will not mention INFO, and anyone who mails it anyway gets the usage instead.

data.name: WriteItAsTextNote
data.value: Write it as text — newlines become line breaks when it is sent. The same EVE mail markup the usage message takes: <b> <i> <u>, <font size="12"> and <font color="#ffc8a84b"> — colours are ARGB, so the alpha pair is not optional. Whitespace on its own does not count as filled in.

data.name: WhatHelpSendsAndNote
data.value: What HELP sends, and what goes back with anything this store could not understand. The default explains ordering in general; a store with its own rules — one hull per buyer, a fixed price, a programme with conditions — is better off saying so in its own words than sending instructions that do not apply.

data.name: UseACustomUsage
data.value: Use a custom usage message for this store

data.name: WriteItAsTextNote2
data.value: Write it as text — newlines become line breaks when it is sent. EVE mail markup: <b> <i> <u>, <font size="12"> and <font color="#ffc8a84b"> — colours are ARGB, so the alpha pair is not optional. Item and character links are <a href="showinfo:TYPEID"> and <a href="showinfo:1373//CHARACTERID">. Spaces are kept as written; HTML entities are not decoded and will be drawn as typed.
